context_units.text: Do not be jealous of the wife at your bosom, and do not teach her an evil lesson against yourself.
Do not give your soul to a woman so that she steps upon your strength.
Do not encounter a woman who acts as a courtesan, lest you fall into her traps.
Do not spend your time with a female musician, lest you be caught by her undertakings.
Do not study a virgin closely, lest you stumble into penalties on her account.
Do not give your soul to prostitutes, so that you do not lose your inheritance.
Do not look around in the streets of a city, or wander in its deserted places.
Turn your eye away from a shapely woman, and do not study another’s beauty closely. Many have been led astray by a woman’s beauty, and from it affection is kindled like fire.
Do not sit at all with a married woman or share a wine feast with her, lest your soul turn toward her and you slip in your spirit into destruction.
Do not abandon an old friend, for a recent one is not his equal. A new friend is new wine; when it has aged, you will drink it with gladness.
Do not envy a sinner’s glory, for you do not know what his downfall will be.
Do not take pleasure in the prosperity of the ungodly; remember that even down to Hades they will certainly not be acquitted.

Keep far away from a person who has authority to kill, and you will certainly not suspect the fear of death. If you do approach him, do not offend, so that he does not take away your life. Recognize that you are crossing among traps and walking upon a city’s battlements.
To the best of your strength, take the measure of your neighbors, and seek counsel with the wise.
Let your deliberation be with people of understanding, and let all your discourse be in the law of the Most High.
Let righteous men be your table companions, and let your boast be in the fear of the Lord.
A work will be praised through the hand of craftsmen, and a leader of the people is wise through his speech.
A talkative man is feared in his city, and one who is rash in his speech will be hated.
A wise judge will instruct his people, and the government of an understanding person will be orderly.
As the judge of a people is, so are his ministers; as the ruler of a city is, so are all who inhabit it.
An uninstructed king will destroy his people, but a city will be settled through the understanding of its rulers.
Authority over the earth is in the Lord’s hand, and at the right time He will raise up the fitting person over it.
A man’s prosperity is in the Lord’s hand, and He will place His glory upon the face of a scribe.
Do not bear anger toward your neighbor over every wrong, and do nothing by acts of insolence.
Pride is hateful before the Lord and human beings, and injustice is offensive to both.
Sovereignty passes from nation to nation because of injustices, acts of insolence, and money.
Why are earth and ashes proud? For even in life I have cast out his entrails.
A long illness—the physician mocks it. A king today, and tomorrow he will die.
For when a person dies, he will inherit creeping things, beasts, and worms.
The beginning of a person’s pride is to withdraw from the Lord; his heart has departed from his Maker.
For the beginning of pride is sin, and the one who holds it fast will rain down abomination. Therefore the Lord made the calamities extraordinary and overthrew them completely.
The Lord pulled down the thrones of rulers and seated the gentle in their place.
The Lord plucked out the roots of nations and planted the humble in their place.
The Lord overthrew the lands of nations and destroyed them down to the foundations of the earth.
He removed some from among them and destroyed them, and made their memory cease from the earth.
Pride was not created for human beings, nor furious anger for those born of women.

What offspring is honorable? Human offspring. What offspring is honorable? Those who fear the Lord. What offspring is dishonorable? Human offspring. What offspring is dishonorable? Those who transgress commandments.
Among brothers their leader is honored, and those who fear the Lord are honored in His eyes.
Rich, renowned, and poor alike—their boast is the fear of the Lord.
It is not right to dishonor an understanding poor person, and it is not fitting to glorify a sinful man.
A dignitary, judge, and ruler will be glorified, but none of them is greater than the one who fears the Lord.
Free people will serve a wise household slave, and a knowledgeable man will not grumble.
Do not be clever about doing your work, and do not glorify yourself in a time of distress.
Better someone who works and has abundance in everything than someone who walks about enjoying glory but lacks bread.
Child, glorify your soul with gentleness, and give it honor according to its worth.
Who will justify the one who sins against his own soul? Who will glorify the one who dishonors his own life?
A poor person is glorified for his knowledge, and a rich person is glorified for his wealth.
If someone is honored in poverty, how much more in wealth? If someone is without honor in wealth, how much more in poverty?
The wisdom of a humble person will raise his head and seat him among dignitaries.
Do not praise a man for his beauty or loathe a person for his appearance.
The bee is small among winged creatures, but her product is foremost among sweet things.
Do not boast in the clothing you wear or exalt yourself on a day of glory. For the Lord’s works are wonderful, and His works are hidden from human beings.
Many rulers have sat upon the ground, while someone unsuspected wore a diadem.
Many powerful people have been greatly dishonored, and the renowned were handed into others’ hands.
Do not find fault before investigating; understand first, and then rebuke.
Do not answer before hearing, and do not interrupt in the middle of someone’s words.
Do not quarrel about a matter that is no concern of yours, and do not sit together in the judgment of sinners.

Child, do not let your activities concern too many things. If you multiply them, you will not escape blame; even if you pursue, you will certainly not catch up, and even by running away you will certainly not escape.
There is someone who toils, labors, and hurries, yet is all the more in want.
There is someone slow who needs support, lacking strength and abounding in poverty. Yet the Lord’s eyes looked upon him for good, and He raised him from his low estate
and lifted his head, and many marveled at him.
Good things and bad, life and death, poverty and wealth are from the Lord.
The Lord’s gift remains with the godly, and His good pleasure will prosper for ever.
There is someone who grows rich through his attention and frugality, and this is his allotted reward:
when he says, “I have found rest, and now I will eat from my good things,” he does not know how much time will pass before he leaves them to others and dies.
Stand firm in your covenant, occupy yourself with it, and grow old in your work.
Do not marvel at a sinner’s works, but trust the Lord and remain at your labor. For it is easy in the Lord’s eyes to make a poor person rich quickly and suddenly.
The Lord’s blessing is in the godly person’s reward, and in a swift moment He makes His blessing flourish.
Do not say, “What need do I have, and what good things will be mine from now on?”
Do not say, “I have enough; what harm can come to me from now on?”
On a day of good things, bad things are forgotten; on a day of bad things, good things will not be remembered.
For it is easy before the Lord, on the day of death, to repay a person according to his ways.
An hour’s suffering makes one forget luxury, and at a person’s end his works are revealed.
Call no one happy before his death, and a man will be known in his children.
Do not bring every person into your house, for the deceitful person has many ambushes.
Like a decoy partridge in a basket is the heart of a proud person; like a spy, he watches for a fall.
For he lies in wait, turning good things into bad, and will attach blame to what is choice.
From a spark of fire a bed of coals grows, and a sinful person lies in ambush for blood.
Beware of an evildoer, for he devises evil, lest he give you lasting blame.
Settle a stranger in your house, and he will throw you into disorder with troubles and estrange you from your own people.
If you do good, know to whom you do it, and there will be gratitude for your good deeds.
Do good to a godly person, and you will find repayment; if not from him, then from the Most High.
There will be no good things for the one who persists in evil and the one who gives no alms.
Give to the godly person, and do not support the sinner.

Do good to the humble person, and do not give to the ungodly. Hold back his loaves and do not give them to him, so that he does not use them to overpower you. For you will receive double evils for all the good things you do to him.
For the Most High Himself has hated sinners and will repay the ungodly with retribution.
Give to the good person, and do not support the sinner.
A friend will not be vindicated in prosperity, and an enemy will not remain hidden in adversity.
When a man prospers, his enemies are in grief; when he suffers adversity, even his friend will separate himself.
Never trust your enemy, for as copper corrodes, so does his wickedness.

Even if he humbles himself and walks bowed down, keep your soul alert and guard against him. You will be toward him like someone who has wiped a mirror, and you will know that it has not completely corroded.

Do not station him beside yourself, lest he overthrow you and stand in your place. Do not seat him at your right hand, lest he seek your seat; then in the end you will recognize my words and be pierced by my sayings.
Who will pity a snake-charmer bitten by a serpent, or all those who approach wild beasts?
So it is with the one who approaches a sinful man and becomes entangled in his sins.
He will stay with you for an hour, but if you turn aside, he will certainly not hold firm.
An enemy will make his lips sweet, but in his heart he will plan to throw you into a pit. An enemy will weep with his eyes, but if he finds the occasion, he will not be satisfied with blood.
If evil things meet you, you will find him there before you; as though helping, he will undermine your heel.
He will shake his head and clap his hands, whisper many things, and change his expression.
The one who touches pitch will be stained, and the one who associates with a proud person will become like him.

Do not lift a burden beyond you, and do not associate with someone stronger and richer than you. What fellowship can an earthen pot have with a cauldron? One will strike, and the other will be shattered.
A rich person has done wrong, yet he has added threats; a poor person has been wronged, yet he will add entreaties.
If you are useful, he makes use of you; if you are in want, he will abandon you.
If you have something, he will live with you and empty you out, while he himself takes no trouble.
He needs you, and he will mislead you, smile at you, and give you hope. He will say pleasant things to you and ask, “What do you need?”
He will shame you with his food until he has emptied you out twice or three times, and in the end he will mock you. After this he will see you and abandon you and shake his head at you.
Take care not to be misled or brought low through your folly.
When a powerful person summons you, be retiring, and he will summon you all the more.
Do not thrust yourself forward, lest you be pushed away; do not stand too far off, so that you are not forgotten.
Do not insist on speaking with him as an equal, and do not trust his many words. For through much talk he will test you and examine you as though smiling.
Merciless is the one who does not keep words to himself, and he will certainly not spare you harm and bonds.
Keep watch and take very great care, because you are walking alongside your downfall.
Every living creature loves its like, and every person his neighbor.
All flesh gathers according to kind, and a man will cling to someone like himself.
What fellowship can a wolf have with a lamb? So it is with a sinner and a godly person.
What peace can a hyena have with a dog? What peace can a rich person have with a poor one?
Wild asses in the wilderness are prey for lions; so the poor are feeding grounds for the rich.
Lowliness is an abomination to the proud; so a poor person is an abomination to the rich.
A rich person who is shaken is supported by friends; a lowly person who falls is pushed away still further by friends.

When a rich person stumbles, many support him. He spoke things that should not be spoken, and they justified him. A lowly person stumbled, and they added rebuke; he spoke with understanding, and no place was given him.
A rich person spoke, and everyone fell silent; they raised his word to the clouds. A poor person spoke, and they said, “Who is this?” If he stumbles, they will throw him down all the more.
Wealth is good when no sin accompanies it, and poverty is evil in the mouth of the ungodly.
A person’s heart changes his face, whether for good or for evil.
A cheerful face is the trace of a heart in good circumstances, and finding proverbs requires laborious deliberations.
Happy is the man who has not slipped with his mouth and has not been pierced by grief over sins.
Happy is the one whose soul has not condemned him and who has not fallen away from his hope.
Wealth is not good for a miserly man; what are possessions for a grudging person?
The one who gathers by depriving his own soul gathers for others, and strangers will enjoy his good things.
To whom will the one who is bad to himself be good? He will certainly not rejoice in his possessions.
No one is worse than the one who begrudges himself, and this is the repayment of his evil:
even if he does good, he does it forgetfully, and in the end he reveals his evil.
Evil is the one who begrudges with his eye, turning his face away and disregarding souls.
A greedy person’s eye is not satisfied with its portion, and evil injustice dries up the soul.
An evil eye begrudges bread, and his own table is lacking.
Child, do yourself good according to what you have, and bring offerings worthily to the Lord.
Remember that death will not delay, and the covenant of Hades has not been shown to you.
Before you die, do good to a friend; according to your strength, reach out and give to him.
Do not miss a good day, and do not let your share of a good desire pass you by.
Will you not leave your labors to another, and your toils to the division of an inheritance?
Give and receive, and beguile your soul, for in Hades there is no seeking luxury.
All flesh grows old like a garment, for the covenant from eternity is, “You will surely die.”
Like flourishing foliage on a leafy tree—some it casts down, while other leaves it grows—so is a generation of flesh and blood: one dies, and another is born.
Every decaying work comes to an end, and its maker will depart with it.
Happy is the man who will meditate on wisdom and speak with his understanding,
who considers her ways in his heart and will reflect upon her hidden things.
Go out after her like a tracker, and lie in wait on her paths.
The one who peers through her windows will also listen at her doorways;
the one who lodges near her house will fix a tent peg in her walls.
He will pitch his tent beside her and lodge in a lodging of good things.
He will place his children in her shelter and spend the night beneath her branches.
He will be sheltered by her from the heat and lodge in her glory.
The one who fears the Lord will do this, and the one who holds fast to the law will gain her.
She will meet him like a mother and welcome him like a wife of his youth.
She will feed him bread of understanding and give him water of wisdom to drink.
He will lean upon her and certainly not be shaken; he will hold to her and certainly not be put to shame.
She will raise him above his neighbors and open his mouth in the midst of the assembly.
He will find gladness and a crown of rejoicing, and inherit an everlasting name.
People without understanding will certainly not gain her, and sinful men will certainly not see her.
She is far from pride, and lying men will certainly not remember her.
Praise is not fitting in a sinner’s mouth, because it was not sent from the Lord.
For praise will be spoken in wisdom, and the Lord will cause it to prosper.
Do not say, “Because of the Lord I fell away,” for He will not do the things He hates.
Do not say, “He Himself led me astray,” for He has no need of a sinful man.
The Lord has hated every abomination, and it is not loved by those who fear Him.
He Himself made the human being from the beginning and left him in the hand of his own deliberation.
If you are willing, you will keep the commandments; to act faithfully is a matter of good will.
He has placed fire and water before you; toward whichever you wish, you will stretch out your hand.
Before human beings are life and death, and whichever a person chooses will be given to him.
For the Lord’s wisdom is great; He is strong in dominion and sees all things.
His eyes are upon those who fear Him, and He Himself will know every human deed.
He commanded no one to act ungodly, and He gave no one license to sin.
Do not desire a multitude of useless children, or rejoice in ungodly sons.
Even if they multiply, do not rejoice in them unless the fear of the Lord is with them.
Do not trust in their life or rely on their multitude. For one is better than a thousand, and it is better to die childless than to have ungodly children.
For through one understanding person a city will be settled, but a tribe of lawless people will become desolate.
My eye has seen many such things, and my ear has heard things stronger than these.
In an assembly of sinners fire will be kindled, and in a disobedient nation wrath was kindled.
He did not make atonement for the ancient giants, who rebelled in their strength.
He did not spare Lot’s neighbors, whom He loathed because of their pride.
He did not have mercy on the nation of destruction, those carried away in their sins,
and likewise on the six hundred thousand foot soldiers gathered together in their hardness of heart.
Even if there is one stiff-necked person, it is a wonder if he will be acquitted. For mercy and wrath are with Him; He is mighty in atonements and pours out wrath.
As His mercy is great, so also His rebuke is great; He will judge a man according to his deeds.
A sinner will not escape with his plunder, and a godly person’s endurance will certainly not be left behind.
He will make room for every act of almsgiving; each person will receive according to his deeds.
Do not say, “I will be hidden from the Lord; who will remember me from on high? Among a numerous people I will certainly not be known, for what is my soul in the immeasurable creation?”
Behold, heaven and the heaven of heaven, the abyss and the earth will be shaken at His visitation.
Together the mountains and the foundations of the earth are shaken with trembling when He looks upon them.
Yet no heart will consider these things, and who will ponder His ways?
There is also a tempest that a person will not see, and most of His works are hidden.
Who will announce works of righteousness? Who will wait? For the covenant is far away.
Someone deficient in heart thinks these things; a foolish and wandering man thinks foolish things.
Listen to me, child, and learn knowledge; attend to my words with your heart.
I will disclose instruction by measure and declare knowledge with precision.
By the Lord’s judgment His works have existed from the beginning; from their making He distinguished their portions.
He ordered His works for ever and their dominions through their generations. They neither hungered nor grew weary, and they did not cease from their tasks.
None crowded out its neighbor, and for ever they will not disobey His word.
After these things the Lord looked upon the earth and filled it with His good things.
He covered its face with the life of every living creature, and to it they return.
The Lord created a human being from earth and returned him to it again.
He gave them numbered days and an appointed time, and He gave them authority over the things upon it.
He clothed them with strength like His own and made them according to His image.
He placed the fear of the human being upon all flesh and granted dominion over beasts and winged creatures.
He gave them deliberation, a tongue and eyes, ears and a heart for understanding.
He filled them with discerning knowledge and showed them good things and evil things.
He set His eye upon their hearts to show them the greatness of His works,
and they will praise the holy name, so that they may recount the greatness of His works.
He added knowledge to them and gave them the law of life as an inheritance.
He established an everlasting covenant with them and showed them His judgments.
Their eyes saw the greatness of glory, and their ear heard the glory of His voice.
He said to them, “Beware of every injustice,” and commanded each of them concerning the neighbor.
Their ways are continually before Him; they will not be hidden from His eyes.
He appointed a ruler for each nation, but Israel is the Lord’s portion.
All their works are like the sun before Him, and His eyes are continually upon their ways.
Their injustices were not hidden from Him, and all their sins are before the Lord.
A man’s almsgiving is like a seal with Him, and He will guard human kindness like the pupil of an eye.
After these things He will rise and repay them; He will return their recompense upon their head.
Yet He gave a way back to those who repent and encouraged those whose endurance was failing.
Return to the Lord and leave sins behind; petition Him face to face and lessen your stumbling.
Come back to the Most High, turn away from injustice, and hate abomination intensely.
Who in Hades will praise the Most High in place of the living who give acknowledgment?
From the dead, as from one who does not exist, thanksgiving perishes; the living and healthy will praise the Lord.
How great is the Lord’s mercy and His atonement for those who return to Him!
For human beings cannot have everything, because a son of man is not immortal.
What is brighter than the sun? Yet even it fails; and flesh and blood will conceive evil.
He Himself surveys the power of the height of heaven, but all human beings are earth and ashes.
Delilah said to him, “How can you say, ‘I love you,’ when your heart is not with me? This is the third time you have deceived me and have not told me where your great strength lies.”
She wore him down with her words all night and troubled him until he grew weary to the point of death.

He told her everything from his heart and said to her, “No razor shall come upon my head, for I am a Nazirite of God from my mother’s womb. If I am shaved, my strength will depart from me; I will become weak and be like everyone else.”

Delilah saw that he had told her everything from his heart. She sent and called all the foreigners’ satraps, saying, “Come up this time, for he has told me all his heart.” All the foreigners’ satrapies came up to her, bringing the silver in their hands.
She put him to sleep between her knees, called the barber, and had the seven curls of his head shaved. He began to be humbled, and his strength departed from him.

Delilah said to him, “The foreigners are upon you, Samson!” He awoke from his sleep and said, “I will go out as at other times and shake myself free.” But he did not know that the Lord had departed from him.
The foreigners seized him and dug out his eyes. They brought him down to Gaza, bound him with bronze fetters, and he ground grain in the prison house.
The hair of his head began to grow again after he had been shaved.
“I established a covenant for my eyes, and I will not direct my attention toward a virgin.
What did God apportion from above, and what is the Mighty One’s inheritance from the highest places?
Is it not destruction for the unjust and alienation for those practicing lawlessness?
Will He not see my way and count all my steps?
Son, guard your father’s laws, and do not reject your mother’s ordinances.
Fasten them always upon your soul, and collar them around your neck.
Whenever you walk, take her along and let her be with you; when you sleep, let her guard you, so that when you rise she may converse with you,
because the commandment of law is a lamp and a light, and correction and discipline are life’s way,
to preserve you from a married woman and from an alien tongue’s slander.
Do not let desire for beauty overcome you; do not be hunted by your own eyes, nor seized by her eyelids.
For a prostitute’s price is as much as one loaf, but a woman hunts men’s precious lives.
Will someone bind fire in his bosom without burning his garments?
Or will someone walk on fiery coals without burning his feet?
So is the one who goes in to a married woman: he will not be acquitted, nor will anyone touching her.
It is no wonder if someone is caught stealing, for he steals to fill his appetite when hungry.
But if caught, he will repay sevenfold, and by giving all his possessions he will rescue himself.
But the adulterer, through lack of sense, brings destruction upon his own life;
he bears pains and dishonors, and his reproach will never be wiped away.
For her husband’s anger is full of jealousy; he will not spare on the day of judgment,
he will not trade his enmity for any ransom, nor be reconciled by many gifts.
For she leans out from a window of her house toward the squares,
and whenever she sees among the foolish children a young man lacking sense,
passing by a corner in the passages of her houses
and talking in evening darkness, when night is still and murky,
the woman meets him, with a prostitute’s appearance, making young men’s hearts fly away.
She is fluttering with excitement and dissolute; her feet do not rest in the house.
For at one time she roams outside, and at another she lies in wait in the squares, at every corner.
Then she took hold of him and kissed him; with a shameless face she addressed him:
“I have a peace sacrifice; today I am paying my vows.
For this reason I came out to meet you; longing for your face, I have found you.
I have stretched my bed with bands and spread it with double-sided rugs from Egypt.
I have sprinkled my bed with saffron and my house with cinnamon.
Come, let us enjoy affection until dawn; come here, let us roll in love.
For my husband is not at home; he has gone on a long journey,
taking a pouch of silver in his hand; after many days he will return to his house.”
She led him astray with much conversation and drove him off course with snares from her lips.
He followed her, made a fool, as an ox is led to slaughter and as a dog to bonds,
or as a deer struck in the liver by an arrow. He hurries like a bird into a trap, not knowing that he runs for his life.
Now therefore, son, listen to me, and attend to my mouth’s sayings.
Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways.
For she has wounded and brought down many, and those she has murdered are beyond counting.
Her house is ways to Hades, leading down to death’s chambers.
Better a man who reproves than a stiff-necked man; for when the latter suddenly burns, there is no healing.
When the righteous are praised, peoples will rejoice; but when the impious rule, men groan.
When a man loves wisdom, his father rejoices; but one who tends prostitutes will destroy wealth.
A righteous king raises up a country, but a lawless man tears it down.
One who prepares a net before his own friend’s face wraps it around his own feet.
For a sinning man there is a great snare, but a righteous person will be in joy and gladness.
A righteous person knows how to judge for the needy, but the impious person will not understand knowledge, and a poor person has no discerning mind.
Pestilent men set a city ablaze, but wise people turned away wrath.
A wise man judges nations, but a worthless man who becomes angry is laughed at and does not shrink back.
Men sharing in bloodshed will hate a holy person, but the upright will seek his life.
A fool brings out all his anger, but a wise person stores it up portion by portion.
When a king listens to an unjust word, all those under him are lawless.
The heart delights in perfumes and wines and incense, but the life is torn apart by misfortunes.
Do not abandon your friend or an ancestral friend, and do not enter your brother’s house when misfortune strikes you; a nearby friend is better than a brother dwelling far away.
Do not let your heart envy sinners, but be in the fear of the Lord the whole day;
for if you keep these things, you will have offspring, and your hope will not depart.
A psalm of Asaph. How good God is to Israel, to those upright in heart!
But my feet were almost shaken; my steps were nearly poured out.
For I envied the lawless, beholding sinners’ peace,
for there is no refusal at their death, and firmness in their scourging.
They are not in human toils, and they will not be scourged with humans.
Therefore arrogance seized them; they wrapped themselves in their injustice and ungodliness.
Their injustice will come out as though from fat; they passed into a disposition of heart.
They devised and spoke in wickedness; they spoke injustice against the height.
They set their mouth toward heaven, and their tongue passed over the earth.
Therefore my people will return here, and full days will be found for them.
And they said, “How did God know? And is there knowledge in the Most High?”
Behold, these are sinners, and they prosper; for the age they took possession of wealth.
And I said, “Then in vain I made my heart righteous and washed my hands among the innocent;
and I became scourged all day, and my rebuke comes in the mornings.”
If I were saying, “I will recount it thus,” behold, I would have broken faith with the generation of Thy sons.
And I undertook to understand this; it is toil before me,
until I enter God’s sanctuary and understand their last things.
Nevertheless, because of their deceits Thou didst set things for them; Thou didst cast them down when they were lifted up.
How they became desolate suddenly! They failed; they perished through their lawlessness.
Like the dream of someone awakening, Lord, in Thy city Thou wilt count their image as nothing.
Wine is undisciplined, and drunkenness insolent, and everyone who mingles with it will not be wise.
A king’s threat does not differ at all from a lion’s wrath, and one who provokes him sins against his own life.
It is glory for a man to turn away from abuse, but every fool entangles himself in such things.
One who walks with the wise will be wise, but one who walks with fools will be known.

And these are the ordinances and judgments which the Lord commanded the sons of Israel in the wilderness, when they came forth out of the land of Egypt: Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.
And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your strength.
And these words, which I command you this day, shall be in your heart and in your soul.
And you shall teach them to your sons, and speak of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk in the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.
And you shall bind them for a sign upon your hand, and it shall be immovable before your eyes.
And you shall write them upon the doorposts of your houses and of your gates.
I wrote to you in the letter not to associate with sexually immoral people,
not at all meaning the sexually immoral people of this world, or the greedy and grasping, or idolaters; otherwise you would have to leave the world.

But now I have written to you not to associate with anyone who is called a brother if he is sexually immoral or greedy or an idolater or abusive or a drunkard or grasping—not even to eat with such a person.
For what have I to do with judging those outside? Do you not judge those inside?
But God will judge those outside. Remove the wicked person from among yourselves.
The words of a wise person’s mouth are gracious, but a fool’s lips will drown him.
The beginning of his mouth’s words is folly, and the end of his speech is evil wandering.
The fool multiplies words. A person did not know what happened, and who will tell him what will be after him?
The toil of fools will weary them, the one who did not know how to go to the city.
Woe to you, city, whose king is young and whose rulers eat in the morning!
Blessed are you, land, whose king is a son of free people and whose rulers will eat at the proper time in strength and will not be ashamed!
A word in a man’s heart is deep water, and a river springs up, a fountain of life.
To admire the face of the impious is not good, nor is it holy to turn aside what is just in judgment.
A fool’s lips lead him into evils, and his rash mouth calls upon death.
A fool’s mouth is ruin for him, and his lips are a trap for his life.
Fear casts down the lazy, and the lives of womanish men will hunger.
The king said, “Divide the living nursing child in two. Give half of it to this woman and half of it to this woman.”

The woman whose son was alive answered the king, for her womb was stirred for her son. She said, “Please, my lord, give her the child! You must not put him to death!” But the other said, “He shall belong to neither me nor her. Divide him.”
The king answered, “Give the child to the woman who said, ‘Give it to her,’ and you must not put him to death. She is his mother.”
All Israel heard this judgment the king had given, and they feared the king, for they saw that God’s discernment was within him to carry out justice.
and cried out, “The name of the great Lord will be blessed for ever, because wisdom and majesty belong to Him.
He changes seasons and times, transfers kings and appoints them, gives wisdom to the wise and understanding to those who possess knowledge,
reveals deep and dark things, knows what is in darkness and what is in light, and with Him is a dwelling.
To Thee, Lord of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, because Thou hast given me wisdom and prudence. Now Thou hast shown me everything I requested, to disclose these things to the king.”
For I set all this upon my heart, and my heart saw all this: the righteous, the wise and their works are in God’s hand. A person knows neither love nor hatred; everything lies before them.
You shall not hate your brother in your mind; you shall surely reprove your neighbour, and you shall not bear sin because of him.
And your hand shall not take vengeance, neither shall you remain angry with the sons of your people; and you shall love your neighbour as yourself; I am the Lord.
Everyone high of heart is unclean before God, and one who unjustly puts hands into a hand will not be acquitted.
An impious person flees when no one pursues, but a righteous person is confident like a lion.
Through the sins of the impious, disputes arise, but a prudent man will extinguish them.
A man vigorous in impieties extorts the poor. Just like a violent and useless rain,
so those who abandon the law praise impiety, but those who love the law surround themselves with a wall.
And Abraham answered and said, “Now I have begun to speak to the Lord, though I am earth and ashes.
If the fifty righteous lack five, wilt Thou destroy the whole city for the five?” And He said, “I will surely not destroy it if I find forty-five there.”
And he spoke to Him yet again and said, “What if forty are found there?” And He said, “I will surely not destroy it for the sake of the forty.”
And he said, “I pray Thee, Lord, allow me to speak: what if thirty are found there?” And He said, “I will surely not destroy it if I find thirty there.”
And he said, “Since I may speak to the Lord, what if twenty are found there?” And He said, “I will surely not destroy it for the sake of the twenty.”
And he said, “I pray Thee, Lord, allow me to speak once more: what if ten are found there?” And He said, “I will surely not destroy it for the sake of the ten.”
Do not trust in rulers and in sons of men who have no salvation.
His spirit will go out, and he will return to his earth; on that day all their reasonings will perish.
This one will die in the strength of his integrity, entirely comfortable and prosperous;
his inward parts are full of fat, and his marrow spreads abundantly.
But another dies in bitterness of soul, never having eaten anything good.
Together they sleep upon the earth, and decay covered them.
Hades below grew bitter on meeting you. All the giants who ruled the earth rose together for you, those who raised all the nations’ kings from their thrones.
They will all answer and say to you, ‘You too were captured as we were, and were numbered among us.’
Your glory went down to Hades, your abundant gladness. They will spread decay beneath you, and your covering is a worm.
How the dawn-bearer who rises in the morning fell from heaven! The one dispatching to all the nations was shattered to earth.
You said in your mind, ‘I will ascend to heaven, set my throne above heaven’s stars, and sit on a high mountain, upon the high mountains toward the north.
I will ascend above the clouds; I will be like the Most High.’
But now you will descend to Hades and to the earth’s foundations.
For the ancient inhabitants of Thy holy land,
whom Thou didst hate for practicing the most detestable things— works of sorcery and unholy rites,
merciless murders of children, and an entrail-devouring feast of human flesh and blood— initiates from the midst of a ritual company,
and parents who were murderers of helpless lives, Thou didst will to destroy by the hands of our fathers,
so that the land most precious to Thee of all might receive a worthy settlement of God’s children.
And you shall eat and be filled, and bless the Lord your God upon the good land which He has given you.
Take heed unto yourself, lest you forget the Lord your God, and fail to keep His commandments, and His judgments, and His ordinances which I command you this day;
lest, when you have eaten and are filled, and have built good houses and dwelt in them,
and your herds and your flocks are multiplied, and your silver and your gold are multiplied, and all that you have is multiplied,
you become lifted up in heart, and forget the Lord your God, who brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage;

who led you through that great and fearful wilderness, wherein were biting serpents, and scorpions, and thirst, where there was no water; who brought forth for you a spring of water out of the sheer rock;
who fed you with manna in the wilderness, which your fathers did not know, to afflict you and to test you, and to do you good in your latter days.
Do not say in your heart: My strength and the might of my hand have gotten me this great wealth.
And you shall remember the Lord your God, for He gives you strength to gain wealth, that He may establish His covenant which the Lord sware unto your fathers, as at this day.
Insolence leads before ruin, and evil-mindedness before a fall.
Mary said, “My soul magnifies the Lord,
and my spirit rejoiced in God my Savior,
because He looked upon the lowly condition of His servant. For behold, from now on all generations will call me blessed,
because the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is His name.
His mercy is for generations and generations upon those who fear Him.
He has performed a mighty deed with His arm; He scattered the proud in the thought of their heart.
He brought rulers down from thrones and raised up the lowly.
He filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty.
He helped Israel His servant, remembering mercy,
as He spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and his offspring forever.”
God, with our ears we heard; our fathers announced to us the work Thou didst in their days, in ancient days.
Thy hand destroyed nations, and Thou didst plant our fathers; Thou didst afflict peoples and cast them out.
For they did not inherit the land by their sword, and their arm did not save them, but Thy right hand, Thine arm and the light of Thy face, because Thou didst delight in them.
for Thou hast upheld my judgment and my cause; Thou sattest on a throne, Thou who judgest righteousness.
Thou didst rebuke nations, and the ungodly one perished; Thou didst erase their name for ever and for the age of the age.
The enemy’s swords failed utterly, and Thou didst pull down cities; their memory perished with a noise.
A psalm of David. Lord, who will sojourn in Thy dwelling, and who will encamp on Thy holy mountain?
One who walks blamelessly and works righteousness, speaking truth in his heart,
who did not act deceitfully with his tongue, nor do evil to his neighbor, and did not take up reproach against those nearest him.
One who acts wickedly is held in contempt before him, but he honors those who fear the Lord; one who swears to his neighbor and does not set it aside.
He did not lend his silver at interest and did not take gifts against innocent people. The one who does these things will never be shaken.
Thus says the Lord: Let no wise man boast in his wisdom, let no strong man boast in his strength, and let no rich man boast in his wealth,
but let whoever boasts boast in this: understanding and knowing that I am the Lord, doing mercy and judgment and righteousness upon the earth, because in these is My will, says the Lord.
There was a small city with few people in it; a great king might come against it, surround it and build great siegeworks against it,
and he might find in it a poor wise man, who will deliver the city by his wisdom; yet no one remembered that poor man.
I said, Wisdom is better than strength; yet the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.
The words of the wise, heard quietly, are better than the shouting of rulers in follies.
Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner will destroy much good.
Peter opened his mouth and said, “Truly I understand that God shows no partiality,
but in every nation, whoever fears Him and practices righteousness is acceptable to Him.
An intelligent household servant will rule foolish masters, and divide portions among brothers.
Better is a man in dishonor who serves himself than one who clothes himself in honor but needs bread.
The righteous has compassion on the lives of his animals, but the inward affections of the impious are merciless.
One who works his own land will be filled with loaves, but those who pursue empty things lack understanding.
Let your adornment not be the outward kind—braiding hair, putting on gold ornaments, or dressing in garments—
but the hidden person of the heart, in the imperishable beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is very precious before God.
One who thrusts discipline away hates himself, but one who keeps rebukes loves his own life.
The fear of God is discipline and wisdom, and the beginning of glory will answer her.
A good name is more desirable than much wealth, and good favor is above silver and gold.
Rich and poor met one another, and the Lord made both.
A resourceful person, seeing an evil person severely punished, is himself instructed, but fools passed by and were penalized.
The offspring of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and wealth and glory and life.
Why did possessions come to a fool? For one lacking heart will not be able to acquire wisdom.
When they came in, he saw Eliab and said, “Surely His anointed is before the Lord.”

The Lord said to Samuel, “Do not look at his appearance or the bearing of his height, for I have treated him as nothing. God does not see as a human looks: a human looks at the face, but God looks at the heart.”
And why are you anxious about clothing? Observe the lilies of the field, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin.
Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory clothed himself like one of these.
If God so clothes the grass of the field, which exists today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, will He not much more clothe you, people of little faith?
One who answers a word before hearing it—it is foolishness and reproach for him.
Nicodemus, who had come to Him earlier and was one of them, said to them,
“Does our Law judge a person unless it first hears from him and knows what he does?”
As one who grasps a dog’s tail, so is one who presides over another’s dispute.
Better a handful of rest than two handfuls of toil and resolve of spirit.
Again I turned and saw futility beneath the sun.

There is one person with no second, with neither son nor brother. There is no end to all his toil, and his eye is not filled with wealth. For whom am I toiling and depriving my soul of goodness? This too is futility and a grievous distraction.
A song of the ascents. For Solomon. Unless the Lord builds a house, those building it have labored in vain. Unless the Lord guards a city, the watchman has kept awake in vain.
It is vain for you to rise early, to get up after sitting down, you who eat bread of pain, when He gives sleep to His beloved ones.
The Lord puts to death and gives life; He brings down to Hades and brings up.
The Lord makes poor and makes rich; He humbles and raises high.
He raises the needy from the earth and lifts the poor from the dung heap, to seat them with rulers of peoples and grant them a throne of glory as their inheritance,
Then He told them a parable: “The land of a certain rich man yielded abundantly.
And he reasoned within himself, saying, ‘What shall I do, since I have nowhere to gather my crops?’
And he said, ‘This is what I will do: I will pull down my storehouses and build larger ones, and gather all the grain and my goods there.
And I will say to my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Rest, eat, drink, be glad!”’
But God said to him, ‘Fool, this very night they demand your soul from you; and the things you have prepared—whose will they be?’
So it is with the one who stores up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.”
Hope in the Lord and show kindness; settle in the land, and you will be pastured on its wealth.
Delight yourself in the Lord, and He will give you the requests of your heart.
Reveal your way to the Lord; hope in Him, and He will act.
He will bring out your righteousness like light, and your judgment like noon.
Submit to the Lord and beseech Him; do not be provoked to envy by one prospering in his way, by a person committing lawless deeds.
The Lord’s blessing is upon the head of the righteous; it makes rich, and sorrow in the heart will certainly not be added to it.
The sinner provoked the Lord. According to the abundance of his anger, he will not seek out; God is not before him.
His ways are profaned at every time; Thy judgments are removed from before him; he will lord it over all his enemies.
For he said in his heart, “I will certainly not be shaken, from generation to generation, without adversity.”
Consider God’s works, for who can put in order the one whom God has twisted?
On a day of goodness, live in good; on a day of evil, consider: God has made this in accord with that concerning speech, so that human beings may find out nothing that comes after them.
But by your hardness and unrepentant heart, you store up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and revelation of God’s righteous judgment,
who will repay each according to his works:
to those who, through perseverance in good work, seek glory and honor and incorruptibility, eternal life;
but to those acting from selfish ambition, who disobey the truth but obey unrighteousness, wrath and fury,
A name is better than good oil, and the day of death than the day of one’s birth.
Better to go to a house of mourning than to a house of drinking, for this is the end of every human being, and the living will take it to heart.
A crooked heart did not cling to me; when the evil one turned away from me, I did not know him.
The one secretly speaking against his neighbor I used to drive away; with a proud eye and an insatiable heart, with that one I did not eat.
My eyes were on the faithful of the land, that they might sit with me; the one walking in a blameless way used to minister to me.
One practicing arrogance did not dwell within my house; one speaking unjust things did not prosper before my eyes.
Have mercy on me, Lord, for a man trampled me; fighting all day, he afflicted me.
My enemies trampled me all day, for many are those fighting me from a height.
By day I will fear, but I will hope in Thee.
In God I will praise my words all day. In God I have hoped; I will not fear. What will flesh do to me?
All day they detested my words; all their thoughts against me are for evil.
They will sojourn and conceal themselves; they will watch my heel, just as they waited for my soul.
Son, do not let ungodly men lead you astray; do not agree if they invite you, saying,
Come with us; share in bloodshed. Let us hide a righteous man in the earth unjustly;
let us swallow him alive like Hades and remove his memory from the earth.
Let us seize his costly property and fill our houses with spoils.
Cast your lot among us; let us all obtain a common purse, and let there be one moneybag for us.
Do not walk in the way with them; turn your foot away from their paths,
for their feet run toward evil, and they are quick to shed blood.
For nets are not unjustly stretched out for winged creatures.
For those who share in murder store up evils for themselves, and the overthrow of lawless men is evil.
These are the ways of all who carry out lawless deeds, for through ungodliness they take away their own life.
So also the tongue is a small member and boasts great things. Look how small a fire sets so great a forest ablaze!
And the tongue is a fire. The tongue is established among our members as a world of unrighteousness, staining the whole body, setting the wheel of life ablaze, and itself set ablaze by Gehenna.
Go to the ant, sluggard; see its ways and emulate them, and become wiser than it.
For although it has no cultivated field, and has no one forcing it, and is under no master,
it prepares its food in summer and makes abundant provision at harvest.
Or go to the bee and learn how industrious she is, and how nobly she performs her work,
whose labors kings and private people use for health; she is desired by everyone and held in esteem.
Although weak in bodily strength, she was advanced because she honored wisdom.
How long will you remain lying down, sluggard? When will you rise from sleep?
You sleep a little, sit a little, doze a little, and clasp your chest with your hands a little;
then poverty arrives beside you like an evil traveler, and want like a good runner.
Do not be hasty with your mouth, and do not let your heart hurry to bring out a word before God, for God is in heaven and you are on earth. Therefore let your words be few.
For a dream comes with much distraction, and a fool’s voice with many words.
Whenever you vow a vow to God, do not delay paying it, for there is no delight in fools. Pay whatever you vow.
Better that you do not vow than that you vow and do not pay.
Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not say before God, “It was ignorance,” lest God become angry at your voice and destroy the works of your hands.
For with many dreams come futilities and many words; therefore fear God.
The Lord knows the ways of the blameless, and their inheritance will last for ever.
They will not be put to shame in an evil time, and in days of famine they will be filled.
For sinners will perish; the Lord’s enemies, as soon as they are glorified and exalted, vanished away like smoke—they vanished.
The sinner borrows and will not repay, but the righteous person has compassion and gives.
For those blessing him will inherit the land, but those cursing him will be destroyed.
But when this corruptible puts on incorruption and this mortal puts on immortality, then the written saying will come to pass: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”
“Where, death, is your victory? Where, death, is your sting?”
The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work, knowing that your labor is not empty in the Lord.
Do not boast of things for tomorrow, for you do not know what the coming day will bear.
They finished their life amid good things and fell asleep in the rest of Hades.
A weeping enemy agrees to everything with his lips, but in his heart devises deceits;
if the enemy entreats you with a loud voice, do not be persuaded, for seven evils are in his life.
One who hides enmity establishes deceit, but one well known in councils discloses his own sins.
One who digs a pit for his neighbor will fall into it, and one who rolls a stone rolls it upon himself.
A false tongue hates truth, but an unrestrained mouth makes disorders.
Do not boast before a king, and do not station yourself in the places of rulers;
for it is better for you to be told, “Come up to me,” than for him to humble you before a ruler. Say what your eyes have seen.
Woe to those drawing sins as with a long cord and lawless deeds as with the strap of a heifer’s yoke,
who say, “Let what He will do approach quickly, so that we may see, and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel come, so that we may know!”
Woe to those calling evil good and good evil, making darkness light and light darkness, making bitter sweet and sweet bitter!
Woe to those who are discerning in their own judgment and knowledgeable in their own view!
Woe to your strong ones who drink wine and the powerful who mix strong drink,
who justify the ungodly for gifts and take away the righteous person’s right!
Whoever receives you receives Me, and whoever receives Me receives the One who sent Me.

Whoever receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward, and whoever receives a righteous person in the name of a righteous person will receive a righteous person’s reward.
And whoever gives one of these little ones even a cup of cold water in the name of a disciple, truly I tell you, will certainly not lose his reward.”
If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.
If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do the same.
If you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners to receive the equivalent back.
But love your enemies, do good, and lend, expecting nothing back. Your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, because He is kind to the ungrateful and evil.
Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
Repay no one evil for evil. Take thought for what is honorable before all people.
If possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with all people.
Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but make room for wrath; for it is written, “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”
But if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink; for by doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head.
Do not be conquered by evil, but conquer evil with good.
Do not be deceived; God is not mocked. For whatever a person sows, that he will also reap.
For the one who sows into his own flesh will reap corruption from the flesh, but the one who sows into the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
And let us not grow weary in doing good, for in the proper season we will reap, if we do not give up.
So then, as we have opportunity, let us do good to everyone, especially to those of the household of faith.
For Thou art not a God who desires lawlessness, nor will an evildoer sojourn with Thee.
The lawless will not remain before Thine eyes; Thou didst hate all who work lawlessness.
Thou wilt destroy all who speak falsehood; the Lord abhors a man of bloodshed and deceit.
One who blocks his ears from hearing the weak will himself also call, and there will be no one listening.
Let a friend be yours at all times, and let brothers be useful in times of need; for this is why they are born.
Wealth adds many friends, but the poor person is abandoned even by the friend he has.
A false witness will not be unpunished, and one who accuses unjustly will not escape.
Many attend the faces of kings, but every evil person becomes a reproach to a man.

Everyone who hates a poor brother will also be far from friendship. A good thought will draw near to those who know it, and an intelligent man will find it. One who does many evils brings wickedness to completion, and one who provokes words will not be saved.
Do not dine with a begrudging man, and do not desire his foods,
for as if someone swallowed a hair, so he eats and drinks.
Do not bring him in to yourself and eat your morsel with him, for he will vomit it and ruin your good words.
If the iron falls out and he has troubled the face, he will strengthen his forces; and wisdom is the advantage of the courageous man.
If the snake bites without a whispered charm, there is no advantage for the charmer.
Together all my enemies whispered against me; against me they devised evils for me.
They laid a lawless word against me: “Can it be that the one lying down will not rise again?”
For even the man of my peace, in whom I hoped, who ate my loaves, magnified treachery against me.
All who pass along the road clapped their hands at you. They hissed and shook their heads at Daughter Jerusalem: “Is this the city they will call a crown of glory, the gladness of all the earth?”
All your enemies opened their mouths against you. They hissed and gnashed their teeth; they said, “We have swallowed her! Indeed, this is the day we expected; we found it, we saw it!”
Do not be deceived: “Bad company corrupts good habits.”
Do not be a companion to a quick-tempered man, and do not lodge with an angry friend,
lest you learn his ways and take nooses for your own life.
Do not become unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what sharing is there between righteousness and lawlessness, or what fellowship between light and darkness?
And what harmony is there between Christ and Beliar, or what portion does a believer have with an unbeliever?

And what agreement is there between God’s temple and idols? For we are the temple of the living God, just as God said: “I will dwell in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people.
Therefore come out from their midst and be separated, says the Lord, and do not touch anything unclean; and I will receive you.
And I will be a Father to you, and you will be sons and daughters to Me, says the Lord Almighty.”
My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with acts of favoritism.
For if a man with gold rings and splendid clothing enters your gathering, and a poor person in filthy clothing also enters,
and you pay attention to the one wearing splendid clothing and say, “You sit here in a good place,” but say to the poor person, “You stand, or sit there beneath my footstool,”
have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?
Listen, my beloved brothers: has not God chosen those poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom He promised to those who love Him?
But you have dishonored the poor person. Is it not the rich who oppress you and drag you into courts?
Do they not blaspheme the good name called over you?
When the heart rejoices, the face flourishes, but when it is in sorrows, the face grows gloomy.
An upright heart seeks discernment, but the mouth of the uneducated will know evil things.
All the time the eyes of evil people expect evils, but good people rest quietly continually.
The hearts of the righteous meditate on faithful things, but the mouth of the impious answers evil things.
He told a parable to those who had been invited, noticing how they chose the foremost places at table. He said to them,
“When someone invites you to a wedding feast, do not recline in the foremost place. Someone more honored than you may have been invited by him,
and the one who invited you both will come and say to you, ‘Give this man your place.’ Then you will begin, with shame, to occupy the last place.

But when you are invited, go and recline in the last place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he will say to you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will have honor before all who recline at table with you.
For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”
Thus says the Lord: “For three impieties of Israel, and for four, I will not turn away from him, because they sold a righteous person for silver and a poor person for sandals,

which tread upon the earth’s dust. They struck the heads of the poor with their fists and turned aside the way of the humble; a son and his father went in to the same young slave woman, to profane the name of their God,
and, tying their garments with cords, they made hangings next to the altar, and drank wine from extortions in their God’s house.
He will say: “Hear these things now, authorities of Jacob’s house and remaining ones of Israel’s house! Is it not for you to know justice,
you who hate good things and seek evil things, who snatch their skins from them and their flesh from their bones?”
Just as they ate the flesh of My people, flayed their skins from their bones, crushed their bones and divided them into pieces like flesh for a cauldron and meat for a cooking pot,
Treasures will not profit lawless people, but righteousness will rescue from death.
The Lord will not starve a righteous life, but He will overturn the life of the impious.
Poverty humbles a man, but the hands of the courageous make rich.
If evil becomes sweet in his mouth, he will hide it under his tongue;
he will not spare it and will not abandon it, and he will hold it inside his throat.
And he will certainly not be able to help himself; an asp’s gall is in his belly.
Wealth gathered unjustly will be vomited up; an angel will drag it from his house.
Not many of you should become teachers, my brothers, knowing that we will receive a greater judgment.
For we all stumble in many things. If anyone does not stumble in speech, that person is a complete man, able to bridle his whole body also.
And by this we will know that we are from the truth, and we will reassure our heart before Him,
whenever our heart condemns us, because God is greater than our heart and knows all things.
Beloved, if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence toward God,
and whatever we ask we receive from Him, because we keep His commandments and do what is pleasing before Him.
There is an evil I have seen beneath the sun, and it is great upon human beings:

a person to whom God will give wealth, possessions and glory, so that his soul lacks nothing it desires, yet God will not empower him to eat from it, for a stranger will eat it. This is futility and a grievous sickness.

If a man fathers a hundred children and lives many years, however numerous the days of his years, but his soul is not filled with goodness and he has no burial, I said a stillborn child is better off than he,
for it came in futility and goes in darkness, and in darkness its name will be covered,
and though it has not seen the sun or known anything, it has more rest than he.
Even if he lived through courses of a thousand years but saw no goodness, do not all go to one place?
Do not stretch yourself, being poor, to match a rich man, but hold back in your own reflection;
If you fix your eye upon him, he will appear nowhere, for wings like an eagle’s have been prepared for him, and he returns to the house of the one who presides over him.
Whoever loves silver will not be filled with silver; and who has loved a yield in their abundance? This too is futility.
When goodness increased, those who consumed it multiplied. What strength has its possessor except to look at it with his eyes?
Sweet is the slave’s sleep, whether he eats little or much; but being filled with riches does not let him sleep.
A double-tongued man reveals plans in a council, but one faithful in breath conceals matters.
Besides becoming wise, Ecclesiastes also taught the people knowledge; and an ear will trace out an orderly arrangement of proverbs.
Ecclesiastes sought much to find words of delight and something written in uprightness, words of truth.
The words of the wise are like goads and like planted nails, which were given from collections, from one shepherd, and something beyond them.
My son, beware of making many books; there is no limit, and much study is weariness of the flesh.
A merciful man does good to his own life, but the merciless destroys his own body.

And if there is among you one of your brethren in need, within any of your cities in the land which the Lord your God gives you, you shall not withhold the affection of your heart, neither shall you close your hand against your needy brother.
You shall freely open your hands unto him, and shall surely lend him as much as he needs, according to his want.

Take heed unto yourself, lest there be a hidden, lawless thought in your heart, saying: The seventh year, the year of release, draws near; and your eye be evil toward your needy brother, and you give him nothing, and he cry against you unto the Lord, and there be great sin upon you.

You shall freely give unto him, and shall surely lend him as much as he needs; and your heart shall not be grieved when you give unto him. For because of this the Lord your God shall bless you in all your works, and in all that you put your hand unto.
For the needy shall never cease out of the land; therefore I command you to do this thing, saying: You shall freely open your hands unto your poor brother and unto the needy in your land.

Three times in the year shall every male among you appear before the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord shall choose: in the Feast of Unleavened Bread, and in the Feast of Weeks, and in the Feast of the Pitching of Tents. You shall not appear before the Lord your God empty,
but every man according to the ability of your hands, according to the blessing of the Lord your God which He has given you.
Behold, what I have seen to be good and fitting is to eat and drink and see goodness in all one’s toil beneath the sun during the numbered days of life God has given, for that is one’s portion.
Moreover, every person to whom God has given wealth and possessions, and whom He has empowered to eat from them, take his portion and rejoice in his toil—this is God’s gift.
For he will not often remember the days of his life, because God distracts him with the gladness of his heart.
Come, eat your bread with gladness and drink your wine with a good heart, for God has already favored your deeds.
Let your garments be white at all times, and let oil not be lacking on your head.

Enjoy life with the woman whom you have loved, all the days of your futile life that have been given you under the sun, all your futile days; for this is your share in life and in your toil at which you toil under the sun.
Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your strength, for there is no deed, reckoning, knowledge or wisdom in Hades, where you are going.

Again I saw under the sun that the race is not to the swift, nor battle to the mighty, nor bread to the wise, nor wealth to those with understanding, nor favor to those with knowledge; for time and encounter will happen to them all.
For a person does not know his time: like fish caught in an evil net, and birds caught in a snare, so human beings are trapped at an evil time when it falls upon them suddenly.
I hated all my toil with which I toil beneath the sun, because I leave it to the person who comes after me.
Who knows whether he will be wise or foolish? Yet he has authority over all the toil with which I labored and acted wisely beneath the sun. This too is futility.
I turned to bid my heart farewell concerning all the toil with which I had labored beneath the sun,
for a person may toil with wisdom, knowledge and courage, yet will give his portion to someone who did not toil for it. This too is futility and a great evil.
For what comes to a person from all his toil and the resolve of his heart with which he toils beneath the sun?
For all his days are pain, and his distraction is anger; even at night his heart does not sleep. This too is futility.

Lift your eyes to heaven and look at earth below. Heaven was made firm like smoke, but earth will grow old like a garment, and earth’s inhabitants will die like these. My salvation will last for ever, and My righteousness will never fail.
Listen to Me, you who know judgment, My people with My law in your heart. Do not fear people’s reproach or be overcome by their contempt.
For a garment will be consumed by time, and wool eaten by a moth. But My righteousness will last for ever, and My salvation through generations of generations.”
And the Lord God commanded Adam, saying, “You may freely eat from every tree in the garden;
but from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat. For on the day you eat from it, you shall surely die.”
A generation goes, and a generation comes, but the earth stands for ever.
At the beginning Thou, Lord, didst found the earth, and the heavens are works of Thy hands.
They will perish, but Thou wilt remain; all will grow old like a garment. Like a cloak Thou wilt change them, and they will be changed.
But Thou art the same, and Thy years will not fail.
Blessed is the man who did not walk in the counsel of the ungodly, and did not stand in the way of sinners, and did not sit in the seat of pestilent men;
but his will is in the Lord’s law, and on His law he will meditate day and night.
He will be like the tree planted beside the outlets of waters, which will give its fruit in its season, and whose leaf will not fall off; and everything he does will be prospered.
Son, if you receive an utterance of my commandment and hide it within yourself,
your ear will obey wisdom, and you will apply your heart to understanding; you will also apply it to admonishing your son.
for if you call upon wisdom and give your voice to understanding, and seek perception with a loud voice,
and if you seek it like silver and search it out like treasures,
then you will understand the fear of the Lord and find the knowledge of God.
For the Lord gives wisdom, and from His presence come knowledge and understanding.
Now, therefore, son, listen to me.
Happy is the man who will listen to me, and the person who will keep my ways, staying awake at my doors day by day, guarding the posts of my entrances.
For my ways out are ways out to life, and favor is prepared by the Lord.
Blessed is the person who found wisdom, the mortal who saw good sense,
for trading in her is better than treasures of gold and silver.
She is more valuable than costly stones; nothing evil will stand against her. She is readily known to all who approach her, and nothing precious is worthy of her.
For length of life and years of living are in her right hand, and wealth and glory in her left.
Righteousness proceeds from her mouth, and she carries law and mercy on her tongue.
Her ways are good ways, and all her paths are in peace.
She is a tree of life to all who hold her fast, and secure for those who lean on her as on the Lord.

He will come, and it will be: a cloud will shade every place of Mount Zion and everything around her by day, and as of smoke and as of a light of fire burning by night; with all the glory it will be covered.
It will be shade from heat, shelter and concealment from harshness and rain.
Say that wisdom is your sister, and acquire understanding as your familiar companion,
so that she may keep you from an alien and wicked woman, if she catches you with pleasing words.
Wisdom built herself a house, and set seven pillars beneath it.
She slaughtered her own sacrificial animals, mixed her own wine in a mixing-bowl, and prepared her own table.
She sent her own servants, summoning with a lofty proclamation to the mixing-bowl, saying:
“Whoever is foolish, let him turn aside to me!” And to those lacking understanding she said:
“Come, eat of my loaves, and drink wine that I mixed for you.
Leave foolishness, and you will live; seek understanding, so that you may live, and set insight right in knowledge.”
I loved her and sought her out from my youth, and sought to take her as my bride, and became a lover of her beauty.
For she is an unfailing treasure for human beings; those who acquire it enter into friendship with God, commended by the gifts that come from discipline.
Thus says the Lord: “To the eunuchs who keep My Sabbaths, choose what I wish, and hold fast to My covenant,
I will give them in My house and wall a renowned place better than sons and daughters; I will give them an everlasting name, and it will not fail.
For wisdom will not enter a soul that devises evil, nor will she dwell in a body indebted to sin.
For a holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit and depart from senseless reasonings, and will be put to shame when injustice comes upon it.
But to the sinner God said, “Why do you recount My decrees and take up My covenant through your mouth?
But you hated instruction and cast My words behind you.
If you saw a thief, you would run along with him, and you would place your portion with adulterers.
Your mouth multiplied wickedness, and your tongue was weaving deception.
Sitting, you would speak against your brother, and against your mother’s son you would place a stumbling block.
These things you did, and I kept silent; you conceived the lawless thought that I would be like you. I will rebuke you and set it before your face.
Let no one who is tempted say, “I am being tempted by God.” For God cannot be tempted by evil, and He Himself tempts no one.
But each person is tempted when drawn away and enticed by his own desire.
Then desire, after conceiving, gives birth to sin; and sin, when fully grown, gives birth to death.
Do not be led astray, my beloved brothers.
Every good act of giving and every complete gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow from turning.
For this commandment which I command you this day is not excessively burdensome, neither is it far from you.
It is not in heaven above, that you should say, Who shall ascend for us into heaven, and fetch it for us, that we may hear it and do it?
Neither is it beyond the sea, that you should say, Who shall cross for us unto the other side of the sea, and fetch it for us, and make us hear it, that we may do it?
The word is very near you, in your mouth, and in your heart, and in your hands, that you may do it.
Behold, I have set before your face this day life and death, good and evil.

If you obey the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you this day, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all His ways, and to keep His ordinances and His judgments, then you shall live and be many; and the Lord your God shall bless you in all the land into which you go to inherit it.
And if your heart turns aside, and you will not hearken, and you are led astray to bow down unto other gods and serve them,
I declare unto you this day that you shall surely perish, and you shall in no wise be long-lived upon the land which the Lord your God gives you, into which you are crossing the Jordan to inherit it.
I call heaven and earth to witness unto you this day: I have set before your face life and death, the blessing and the curse. Choose life, that you and your seed may live,

to love the Lord your God, to obey His voice, and to cleave unto Him; for this is your life and the length of your days, that you may dwell upon the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers, Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, to give unto them.
But now finish doing it also, so that your eager desire may be matched by completing it out of what you have.
For if the readiness is present, it is acceptable according to what one has, not according to what one does not have.
For it is not that there should be relief for others and affliction for you, but on the basis of equality:
at the present time your abundance is to meet their lack, so that their abundance may also meet your lack, so that there may be equality.
As it is written, “The one with much had no excess, and the one with little had no shortage.”
Do not refrain from doing good to someone in need whenever your hand has the means to help.
Do not say, ‘Go away and come back; tomorrow I will give,’ when you are able to do good, for you do not know what the coming day will bring forth.
Childlessness with virtue is better, for immortality is in its remembrance, because it is recognized both by God and by human beings.
When it is present, people imitate it, and when it has departed, they long for it; throughout the age it marches crowned in triumph, having won the contest for undefiled prizes.
But the prolific multitude of the ungodly will be of no use; from illegitimate shoots it will not send a root deep down, nor establish a secure foundation.
For even if it flourishes in branches for a time, standing insecurely, it will be shaken by wind and uprooted by the force of winds.
Unfulfilled branches will be broken off, and their fruit will be useless, unripe for eating, and fit for nothing.
For children born from unlawful unions are witnesses of wickedness against their parents at their examination.
As he finished speaking all these words, the ground beneath them split apart.
And the earth opened and swallowed them, their households, all the people who were with Korah, and their livestock.
And they and all that belonged to them went down alive to Hades; the earth covered them, and they perished from the midst of the congregation.
And all Israel around them fled at their cry, saying: Lest the earth swallow us!
And fire went out from the Lord and consumed the two hundred fifty men presenting the incense.
And it came to pass, when mankind began to increase upon the earth and daughters were born to them,
that the sons of God saw that the daughters of men were beautiful, and took wives for themselves from all whom they chose.
And the Lord God said, “My Spirit shall not abide in these men for ever, for they are flesh; and their days shall be a hundred and twenty years.”

Now giants were upon the earth in those days, and afterward also, whenever the sons of God went in to the daughters of men and they bore children to them. These were the giants of old, the men of renown.
And the Lord God saw that the wickedness of mankind had multiplied upon the earth, and that each one continually set his heart upon evil all his days.
And God took to heart that He had made man upon the earth, and pondered it.
And God said, “I will blot out from the face of the earth the mankind I have made, together with the cattle, the creeping things, and the birds of heaven; for I am angered that I made them.”
For even at the beginning, when arrogant giants were perishing, the hope of the world took refuge on a raft and left to the age a seed for generation, steered by Thy hand.
And at dawn, the angels urged Lot, saying, “Arise, take your wife and your two daughters whom you have, and depart, so that you do not perish with the lawless deeds of the city.”
And they were troubled; and the angels took hold of his hand, and the hand of his wife, and the hands of his two daughters, because the Lord spared him.

And when they had brought them outside, they said, “Save your own life. Do not look behind you or stand anywhere in the surrounding country. Escape to the mountain, so that you are not swept away with them.”
