And Lot said to them, “I beg you, lord,
for your servant has found mercy before you, and you have shown me your great righteousness by preserving my life. Yet I cannot escape to the mountain, for calamities may overtake me, and I may die.
Behold, this city is near enough for me to flee to, and it is small. There I shall be saved; is it not small? And my soul shall live.”
And he said to him, “Behold, I have regarded your face in this matter also, that I will not overthrow the city of which you have spoken.
So hurry and be saved there; for I can do nothing until you enter it.” Therefore he called the name of that city Zoar.
The sun rose upon the earth, and Lot entered into Zoar.
And the Lord rained upon Sodom and Gomorrah sulphur and fire from the Lord out of the heaven;
and He overthrew those cities, and all the surrounding country, and all that lived in the cities, and all that sprang from the earth.

Yet this was the lawlessness of your sister Sodom: arrogance. In fullness of bread and abundance of wine she and her daughters lived luxuriously. This belonged to her and her daughters, but they did not support the hand of the poor and needy.
They boasted greatly and committed acts of lawlessness before Me, and I removed them as I saw.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
How long with this evil congregation? They grumble before Me; I have heard the sons of Israel’s grumbling that they have directed against you.
Say to them, I live, says the Lord: I will certainly do to you just as you have spoken into My ears.
In this wilderness your bodies shall fall, with your entire registration and those of you counted from twenty years old and upward who grumbled against Me.
You shall certainly not enter the land over which I stretched out My hand to settle you upon it, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
The sons of Israel departed from Rameses for Succoth, about six hundred thousand men on foot, apart from the household company.
A great mixed multitude also went up with them, together with sheep and cattle and livestock in great abundance.

They baked the dough they had brought from Egypt into unleavened hearth-cakes, because it was not leavened. The Egyptians had driven them out, and they could not stay; nor had they prepared provisions for the journey.
The Lord passed before him and proclaimed, “The Lord God, compassionate and merciful, slow to anger, abundant in mercy and true,

preserving righteousness and showing mercy to thousands, taking away lawlessness, injustice, and sins, yet not cleansing the guilty, bringing the fathers’ lawlessness upon children and children’s children to the third and fourth generation.”
Will not all these take up a parable against him and a riddle for his account? They will say, ‘Woe to the one multiplying for himself what is not his—how long?—and heavily weighting his collar!’
For suddenly those biting him will rise, and those plotting against you will awake; you will become their plunder.
Because you despoiled many nations, all the remaining peoples will despoil you, because of human bloodshed and impiety against land, city and all its inhabitants.
But concerning you, beloved, we are convinced of better things—things accompanying salvation—even though we speak this way.
For God is not unjust so as to forget your work and the love you showed toward His name by serving the saints, as you still serve them.
And we desire each of you to show the same diligence toward the full assurance of hope until the end,
so that you may not become sluggish, but imitators of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
Take care not to practice your righteousness before people in order to be seen by them; otherwise you have no reward with your Father in the heavens.

So when you give alms, do not sound a trumpet before you as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and streets, so that people may glorify them. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.
But when you give alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
so that your almsgiving may be in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will repay you.
I am a God drawing near, says the Lord, and not a God far away.
If a person hides in hidden places, will I not see him? Do I not fill the heaven and the earth? says the Lord.
And the earth was shaken and began to tremble; the foundations of the mountains were troubled and shaken because God was angry with them.
Smoke rose in His anger, and fire from His face set things ablaze; coals were kindled from Him.
And He bent heaven and came down, and gloom was beneath His feet.
How great Thy works have become, Lord; Thy reasonings have grown very deep.
A senseless man will not know, and one without understanding will not understand these things:
He stretches the north over nothing and hangs the earth upon nothing,
binding water in His clouds, and no cloud burst beneath it.
He holds the face of a throne, spreading His cloud over it.
He circled a command upon the waters’ face, until the completion of light with darkness.
The pillars of heaven were spread out and were astonished at His rebuke.
By strength He calmed the sea, and by knowledge He wounded the great sea creature.
The bars of heaven have feared Him, and by a command He killed the rebellious dragon.
Behold, these are parts of His way, and we will hear a mere drop of speech concerning Him. But the strength of His thunder—who knows when He will act?”
knowing this first: in the last days scoffers will come with scoffing, walking according to their own desires,
and saying, “Where is the promise of His coming? For ever since the fathers fell asleep, everything continues as it was from the beginning of creation.”
For they willingly overlook this: that heavens existed long ago, and earth was formed out of water and through water by the word of God,
through which the world that then existed was flooded with water and perished.
But the present heavens and earth have been stored up by the same word for fire, kept for the day of judgment and destruction of ungodly people.
But do not let this one thing escape you, beloved: with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day.
The Lord is not slow concerning the promise, as some consider slowness, but is patient toward you, not wishing anyone to perish but all to come to repentance.
The proverbs of Solomon son of David, who reigned in Israel,
for knowing wisdom and discipline and understanding words of good sense,
for receiving turns of speech, understanding true righteousness, and directing judgment rightly,
so that he may give shrewdness to the innocent, perception and thought to a young child.
For a wise person who hears these things will become wiser, and the discerning will acquire guidance,
and understand a comparison and an obscure saying, the utterances of the wise and riddles.

The fear of God is the beginning of wisdom, and good understanding belongs to all who practice it. Reverence toward God is the beginning of perception, but the ungodly will despise wisdom and discipline.
Son, attend to my utterance; apply your ear to my words,
so that your springs do not fail you; keep them in your heart,
for there is life for those who find them and healing for all flesh.
Even without these, they could have fallen at a single breath, pursued by justice and winnowed away by the breath of Thy power; but Thou didst arrange all things by measure and number and weight.
Hallelujah. Of Haggai and Zechariah. Praise the Lord from the heavens; praise Him in the highest places.
Praise Him, all His angels; praise Him, all His powers.
Praise Him, sun and moon; praise Him, all the stars and the light.
Praise Him, heavens of heavens, and the water above the heavens.
Let them praise the Lord’s name, for He spoke, and they came to be; He commanded, and they were created.
He established them for the age and for the age of the age; He set a command, and it will not pass away.
Praise the Lord from the earth, dragons and all deeps,
fire, hail, snow, ice, storm wind—all fulfilling His word,
How great Thy works have become, Lord! Thou madest all things in wisdom; the earth was filled with Thy possession.
Here is the sea, great and spacious; there are creeping things without number, living creatures small with great.
There ships pass, and this dragon, which Thou didst form to play with it.
All wait for Thee to give them food at the right time.
When Thou givest to them, they will gather; when Thou openest Thy hand, all things will be filled with goodness.
When Thou turnest Thy face away, they will be troubled. Thou wilt take back their breath, and they will fail and return to their dust.
Thou wilt send Thy Spirit, and they will be created, and Thou wilt renew the face of the earth.
And God said, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kind: four-footed animals, creeping things, and wild beasts of the earth according to their kind.” And it was so.

And God made the wild beasts of the earth according to their kind, and the cattle according to their kind, and all the creeping things of the earth according to their kinds. And God saw that they were good.

And God said, “Let Us make man in Our image and likeness; and let them rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of heaven, the cattle, all the earth, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth.”
And God made man; in the image of God He made him; male and female He made them.

And God blessed them, saying, “Grow and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of heaven, all the cattle, all the earth, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth.”
And God said, “Behold, I have given you every plant sowing seed upon all the earth, and every tree that bears fruit containing seed. These shall be yours for food.
And to every wild beast of the earth, every bird of heaven, and every creeping thing upon the earth that has life within it, I have given every green plant for food.” And it was so.
And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning: a sixth day.
And God formed man from the dust of the earth, and breathed into his face the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
By the sweat of your face you shall eat your bread, until you return to the earth from which you were taken; for earth you are, and unto earth you shall return.
“For a mortal born of woman is short-lived and full of wrath.
Like a flower that blossomed, he fell away; he fled like a shadow and will not remain.
Didst Thou not take account of this one also, and bring him into judgment before Thee?
For who will be clean from filth? No one.
Even if his life on earth is one day, his months are numbered with Thee; Thou didst set a time, and he will certainly not go beyond it.
And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them, “Grow and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it.
The dread and fear of you shall fall upon every wild beast of the earth, every bird of heaven, everything that moves upon the earth, and every fish of the sea. Into your hands I have given them.
“Every living thing that moves shall be food for you. As I gave the green plants, so I have given you all things.
Behold, I have shown you ordinances and judgments, as the Lord commanded me, that you should do so in the land whither you go to inherit it.

And you shall keep and do them; for this is your wisdom and understanding before all the nations, who shall hear all these ordinances and say: Behold, this great nation is a wise and understanding people.
For what great nation is there whose god draws near unto them, as the Lord our God in all things wherein we call upon Him?
And what great nation is there that has ordinances and judgments as righteous as all this law which I set before you this day?
Through her I will have glory among the crowds, and, though young, honor among elders.
I will be found keen in judgment and will be admired in the sight of rulers.
When I am silent they will wait for me, and when I speak they will pay attention; if I speak at length, they will place a hand upon their mouth.
Fortify her, and she will exalt you; honor her so that she may embrace you,
so that she may give your head a crown of graces and shield you with a crown of delight.
Wherever insolence enters, dishonor is there too, but the mouth of the humble meditates on wisdom.
Make music to our God, make music; make music to our King, make music.
For God is King of all the earth; make music with understanding.
God reigned over the nations; God sits upon His holy throne.
I, Wisdom, have made counsel my dwelling, and I have called upon knowledge and reflection.
The fear of the Lord hates injustice, insolence and arrogance and the ways of wicked people; and I hate the perverted ways of evil people.
Great is our Lord, and great is His strength; His understanding is beyond number.
From heaven the Lord looked down; He saw all the sons of men.
From His prepared dwelling place He looked upon all who inhabit the earth.
He formed their hearts individually; He understands all their deeds.
A king is not saved through a great force, and a giant will not be saved by the abundance of his strength.
A horse is false for salvation, and by the abundance of its power it will not be saved.
Behold, the Lord’s eyes are upon those who fear Him, those who hope in His mercy,
And God said, “Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven to give light upon the earth and to divide the day from the night. Let them serve for signs and seasons, for days and years.
And let them be lights in the firmament of heaven, to shine upon the earth.” And it was so.
And God made the two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night; He made the stars also.
And God set them in the firmament of heaven to shine upon the earth,
to rule the day and the night, and to divide the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good.
An ear hears and an eye sees; both are works of the Lord.
And Adam called his wife’s name Life, because she was the mother of all the living.
And the Lord God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife, and clothed them.
And God said, “Behold, Adam has become as one of Us, knowing good and evil. And now, lest he stretch forth his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever—”
And the Lord God sent him out of the garden of delight to till the earth from which he had been taken.
And He drove Adam out and settled him opposite the garden of delight. And He stationed the cherubim and the flaming sword that turns about, to guard the way to the tree of life.
Hallelujah. Give thanks to the Lord and call upon His name; announce His works among the nations.
Sing to Him and make music to Him; recount all His wonders.
Be praised in His holy name; let the heart of those seeking the Lord rejoice.
Seek the Lord and be strengthened; seek His face continually.
Remember His wonders that He did, His portents and the judgments of His mouth,
offspring of Abraham, His servants, sons of Jacob, His chosen ones.
He is the Lord our God; His judgments are in all the earth.
He remembered His covenant for ever, the word He commanded for a thousand generations,
which He covenanted with Abraham, and His oath to Isaac;
He established it for Jacob as an ordinance and for Israel as an everlasting covenant,
the law which Moses commanded us, an inheritance for the assemblies of Jacob.

These words the Lord spoke unto all your assembly on the mountain, out of the midst of the fire, with darkness, gloom, tempest, and a great voice; and He added no more. And He wrote them upon two tablets of stone, and gave them unto me.
And it came to pass, when you heard the voice out of the midst of the fire, and the mountain burned with fire, that you drew near unto me, all the heads of your tribes and your elders,
and said: Behold, the Lord our God has shown us His glory, and we have heard His voice out of the midst of the fire. This day we have seen that God speaks with man, and he lives.
And now let us not die, for this great fire will consume us; if we hear the voice of the Lord our God any more, we shall die.
For what flesh has heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the midst of the fire, as we have, and shall live?
You shall not wrong your neighbour, neither shall you rob; and the wages of the hired worker shall in no wise remain with you overnight until morning.
You shall not speak evil of the deaf, neither shall you put a stumbling block before the blind; and you shall fear the Lord your God; I am the Lord your God.
You shall do no injustice in judgment; you shall not favour the person of the poor, neither shall you admire the person of the mighty; you shall judge your neighbour in righteousness.
You shall not go about deceitfully among your nation; you shall not conspire against the blood of your neighbour; I am the Lord your God.
For a man’s ways are before God’s eyes, and He watches all his tracks.
When the Most High divided the nations, when He scattered the sons of Adam, He set the bounds of the nations according to the number of the angels of God.
And His people Jacob became the portion of the Lord; Israel, the measured lot of His inheritance.
In Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion of the cohort called the Italian,
devout and fearing God with his whole household, giving many alms to the people and praying to God continually.
About the ninth hour of the day, he clearly saw in a vision an angel of God come in to him and say, “Cornelius.”
He stared at him in fear and said, “What is it, sir?” The angel said to him, “Your prayers and your alms have ascended as a memorial before God.
For the day of the Lord is near against all the nations. Just as you acted, so it will be for you; your recompense will be repaid upon your own head.
Through such works Thou didst teach Thy people that the righteous person must love humanity, and make Thy sons hopeful, because Thou givest repentance for sins.
